questions.stem: How many moles of HCl are in 25 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Volume = 25 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Moles = concentration x volume = 0.1 x 0.025 = 0.0025 mol. Always convert cm³ to dm³ first by dividing by 1000. A very common error is forgetting this conversion and getting an answer 1000 times too large.

questions.stem: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ NaOH is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of HCl. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. What is the concentration of the HCl?
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 0.1 x (25.0/1000) = 0.0025 mol. From the equation, NaOH:HCl is 1:1, so moles of HCl = 0.0025 mol. Concentration of HCl = moles/volume = 0.0025/(20.0/1000) = 0.0025/0.02 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.stem: What volume of 0.5 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid contains 0.1 moles of H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: Volume = moles / concentration = 0.1 / 0.5 = 0.2 dm³ = 200 cm³. Remember to convert dm³ back to cm³ by multiplying by 1000 if the answer requires cm³. 0.2 dm³ x 1000 = 200 cm³.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH reacts with H₂SO₄ in the reaction: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. How many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed?
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 0.2 x 0.025 = 0.005 mol. From the equation, the ratio is 2NaOH : 1H₂SO₄, so moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.005 / 2 = 0.0025 mol. It's crucial to use the molar ratio from the balanced equation. A common error is forgetting the 2:1 ratio and using the same number of moles.

questions.stem: A solution of sodium hydroxide has a concentration of 4.0 g/dm³. What is its concentration in mol/dm³? [Mr of NaOH = 40]
questions.explanation: To convert from g/dm³ to mol/dm³: concentration in mol/dm³ = concentration in g/dm³ / Mr = 4.0 / 40 = 0.1 mol/dm³. This means there are 0.1 moles of NaOH in every dm³ of solution. To go the other way (mol/dm³ to g/dm³), multiply by Mr.
